requirements_slice.system_goal: Prepare the existing backend active slice for safe deep refactor and stable multi-agent execution by reusing the current strict-GRACE boundary and delivering dense development-phase structured observability without business-semantic drift.

in_scope.item: Reuse the existing backend active-slice module cluster for gateway, trace logging, DayBrief, WeekBrief, analytics, and scheduler boundaries.
Close remaining module-contract, module-map, function-contract, and semantic-block gaps on the bounded backend file set.
Add dense development-phase structured observability on exported, orchestration, and side-effect boundaries in the same bounded backend file set.
Keep packet-local read-only evidence separate from the final canonical today-week observability lane.
Materialize feature-local slice docs and a direct-execution wave graph without forcing planner decomposition.

out_of_scope.item: Changing DayBrief, WeekBrief, report-read, scheduler, analytics, scoring, auth, billing, referral, or frontend business semantics.
Repo-wide logging cleanup or a new logging transport or envelope.
Retroactive full decomposition of backend/app/main.py beyond the approved active-slice blocks.

use_case.summary: Reslice the existing backend active-slice canon-sync plus dev-observability program into bounded direct-execution waves without changing business behavior.
use_case.scenario: Targeted backend active-slice files expose stable module contracts, module maps, function contracts where required, and semantic START and END blocks.

Day, Week, gateway, scheduler, analytics, and correlation paths emit dense structured markers on entry, major steps, branches, fallbacks, validation boundaries, exception conversion, and closeout when exercised.
Verifier and reviewer can reconstruct the relevant scenario history from module, function, block, event, correlation_id, and trace_id without guesswork, and the final today-week verdict is explicit.

business_invariants.invariant: No DayBrief, WeekBrief, report-read, scheduler, analytics, auth, billing, referral, or scoring business semantics change in this slice.
The slice reuses the existing backend active-slice module cluster: M-API-GATEWAY, M-TRACE-LOGGING, M-DAY-BRIEF-SERVICE, M-WEEK-BRIEF-SERVICE, M-ANALYTICS-EVENTS, and M-OPS-AUTOMATION.
Within backend/app/main.py only API_GATEWAY_APP_INIT, API_GATEWAY_REPORT_ORCHESTRATION, API_REPORT_DETAIL_ROUTE, API_TODAY_ROUTE, API_DAY_BRIEF_ROUTE, and API_B2C_REPORT_ROUTE are in scope.
Structured observability must reuse log_grace_event(...) and build_grace_log_payload(...) with the current correlation and header model; no new transport or envelope is allowed.
Dense logging is required on exported, orchestration, and side-effect boundaries, not as blanket noise in every pure helper.
backend/app/services/day_brief_validators.py remains a pure validation and repair helper; caller boundaries own observability for validation entry and failure.
Packet-local read-only evidence cannot close the slice; the final canonical today-week lane owns the wave-final observability verdict.

expected_failure_handling.item: Logging emission or JSONL routing failure must not block API, service, or scheduler completion.
Validation, fallback, retry, persistence-boundary, exception-conversion, and closeout branches must emit explicit markers without changing response semantics.
If packet-local runs do not naturally emit scheduler or analytics paths, the packet must record the evidence gap explicitly instead of claiming clean coverage.
W03 is blocked on no-evidence-blocker or unexpected-degradation from the canonical today-week observability review.

success_criteria.criterion: Remaining contract, map, function-contract, and semantic-block gaps are closed across the targeted backend active-slice files without widening scope.
Development-critical entry, major-step, branch, fallback, retry, persistence, exception-conversion, and closeout markers exist on the targeted runtime boundaries.
backend:quick and the targeted active-slice pytest bundle remain green.

Packet-local read-only review can follow emitted Day, Week, report-read, scheduler, and analytics traces by module, function, block, event, correlation_id, and trace_id where those paths are exercised.
The final canonical today-week review returns clean or degraded-but-expected with explicit rationale; unexpected-degradation or no-evidence-blocker blocks acceptance.
Scheduler or analytics non-emission, when a canonical run does not exercise those paths, is explicit and reviewer-visible rather than silent.
